sources.name: MedlinePlus: Lung Diseases
sources.text: When you breathe, your lungs take in oxygen from the air and deliver it to the bloodstream. The cells in your body need oxygen to work and grow. During a normal day, you breathe nearly 25,000 times. People with lung disease have difficulty breathing. Millions of people in the U.S. have lung disease. If all types of lung disease are lumped together, it is the number three killer in the United States. The term lung disease refers to many disorders affecting the lungs, such as asthma, COPD, infections like influenza, pneumonia and tuberculosis, lung cancer, and many other breathing problems. Some lung diseases can lead to respiratory failure. Dept. of Health and Human Services Office on Women's Health

Metabolic Alkalosis Alkalosis— when the pH is greater than 7.45—is any process that causes a net increase in bicarbonate ions in the plasma. A net increase in bicarbonate ions due to loss of hydrogen ions or retention of bicarbonate ions by either the renal or gastrointestinal systems is called metabolic alkalosis ( Figure 20.7 ).
